main_body: Beehive hut: a conical thatched roof (rows 2-56) over a clay/mud wall with an arched doorway (rows 56-78)
top_band: Thatch roof, light straw yellow at the top and mid-gold below, rows ~2-55. It reads as a large sloped roof surface seen from above, with a darker eave line at rows 55-57.
evidence: Reading down the centre column: the dark finial, then banded thatch roof slopes of several tones down to a dark eave edge at rows ~55-57. A dark shadow band sits just under the eave. Below it is a brown clay wall with horizontal grain. A grey stone plinth sits at rows 75-78. The doorway has a lighter lintel and frame, and the dark interior is set back (inset). The roof is a big visible slope, as in the reference houses, so this is a 3/4 building rather than an elevation. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 tones with per-course dark gaps and vertical straw ticks, which gives good texture. The outline is a dark brown tinted to the thatch and wall rather than black. The clay wall has dithered patches and light horizontal streaks, and the plinth has speckle. The wall is a little simpler than the reference stone and timber walls, and the door interior is a flat dark fill, but that area is small. Overall it sits acceptably next to the references.
